reason: The mechanism named in reasoning.so_that is being bypassed, and the bridge says so in as many words. reasoning.so_that is engine-side competitive parity - 'rival OSS serving stacks adopt quantized-by-default loading and tiered KV offload as defaults to keep cost parity' - with reasoning.landing naming SGLang, TensorRT-LLM and TGI. Bridge validation.5fb27e4950a9e4d5 (2026-07-27, dim=because, rel=4) records Kimi K3 shipping as MXFP4 weights with MXFP8 activations produced by quantization-aware training, with no full-precision release to compress at all, and vLLM shipping a loader for that exact format the same day. The row's own conclusion: 'That is the baseline this claim describes arriving from the model side rather than the engine side - the release makes low-bit loading mandatory instead of optional.' If publishers ship QAT-only checkpoints, rivals adopt quantized loading because there is no alternative artifact, not to defend throughput-per-dollar against vLLM, and the prediction would resolve true for a reason its because/given do not contain. The row is careful to bound this ('what today does not show is the same default reaching the smaller checkpoints'), so this is a reframe rather than a retirement.
